```yaml
lines:
  - id: household.h_ctc_odc_claimed
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Number of dependents for whom the child tax credit (and so the additional child tax credit) or the credit for other dependents is claimed (the \"Child tax credit\" and \"Credit for other dependents\" boxes checked in the Dependents section of Form 1040 or 1040-SR)"
    type: Count
    expr:
      op: sum_over
      collection: dependent
      field: dependent.one
      where:
        op: test
        any:
          - {op: test, eq: [dependent.ctc_child, {const: true}]}
          - {op: test, eq: [dependent.odc_person, {const: true}]}
    note: "Counted from the per-dependent results rather than from Schedule 8812 lines 4 and 6, so that this helper does not depend on Schedule 8812 lines that may themselves stop on the disallowance result."
  - id: household.ctc_disallowed_claim
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Form 8862, who must file: your child tax credit, additional child tax credit, or credit for other dependents for a year after 2015 was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error (or you are in a 2- or 10-year period in which these credits can't be taken), and you are claiming the child tax credit, additional child tax credit or credit for other dependents for 2025"
    type: Bool
    expr:
      op: test
      all:
        - {op: test, eq: [household.credit_disallowed, {const: true}]}
        - {op: test, gt: [household.h_ctc_odc_claimed, {const: 0, type: Count}]}
    note: "The pages do not define this interface; it is read as 'an earlier credit was reduced or disallowed and this return claims the CTC, ACTC or ODC', the case in which Form 8862 must be attached or the credit can't be taken. The closed input interface has one combined question (household.credit_disallowed) covering both the EIC and the CTC/ACTC/ODC, so a disallowance of the EIC alone cannot be told apart from one of the CTC/ACTC/ODC; a yes is treated as applying to these credits. The exception for a Form 8862 already filed for 2024 with the credit allowed, and the other exceptions in the Form 8862 instructions, cannot be determined from the supplied inputs and are not encoded."
  - id: household.eic_disallowed_claim
    printed: "(helper)"
    label: "Form 8862, who must file: your EIC for a year after 1996 was reduced or disallowed for any reason other than a math or clerical error (or you are in the 2 or 10 years after a final determination that your EIC claim was due to reckless or intentional disregard of the EIC rules or to fraud), and you would otherwise take the earned income credit for 2025"
    type: Bool
    expr:
      op: test
      all:
        - {op: test, eq: [household.credit_disallowed, {const: true}]}
        - {op: test, eq: [eic.eligible, {const: true}]}
    note: "The pages do not define this interface; it is read as 'an earlier credit was reduced or disallowed and this return would otherwise take the EIC'. eic.eligible is assumed to mean that the filer meets the EIC steps, and is used rather than the credit amount so that the result does not depend on a line that may stop on it. The single combined input (household.credit_disallowed) cannot tell an EIC disallowance from a CTC/ACTC/ODC one; a yes is treated as applying to the EIC. The two exceptions (Form 8862 filed for another year with the EIC allowed and not reduced or disallowed again; taking the EIC without a qualifying child when the only reason for the earlier disallowance was that a child listed on Schedule EIC wasn't your qualifying child) cannot be determined from the supplied inputs and are not encoded."
```

Second transcription's note: The pages do not define this interface; it is read as 'an earlier credit was reduced or disallowed and this return claims the CTC, ACTC or ODC', the case in which Form 8862 must be attached or the credit can't be taken. The closed input interface has one combined question (household.credit_disallowed) covering both the EIC and the CTC/ACTC/ODC, so a disallowance of the EIC alone cannot be told apart from one of the CTC/ACTC/ODC; a yes is treated as applying to these credits. The exception for a Form 8862 already filed for 2024 with the credit allowed, and the other exceptions in the Form 8862 instructions, cannot be determined from the supplied inputs and are not encoded.


Second transcription's note: The pages do not define this interface; it is read as 'an earlier credit was reduced or disallowed and this return would otherwise take the EIC'. eic.eligible is assumed to mean that the filer meets the EIC steps, and is used rather than the credit amount so that the result does not depend on a line that may stop on it. The single combined input (household.credit_disallowed) cannot tell an EIC disallowance from a CTC/ACTC/ODC one; a yes is treated as applying to the EIC. The two exceptions (Form 8862 filed for another year with the EIC allowed and not reduced or disallowed again; taking the EIC without a qualifying child when the only reason for the earlier disallowance was that a child listed on Schedule EIC wasn't your qualifying child) cannot be determined from the supplied inputs and are not encoded.
